title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>

title: Cyber Defense Digital Twins: A Federated Learning and Zero-Trust AI Architecture for Autonomous Threat Prediction and Response
abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>

title: Promise or Precaution: An Exploratory Study of the Performance of OpenEvidence (OE) in Clinical Decision Making in the Global Context.
abstract: Background Clinicians face the challenging task of keeping up with evidence-based literature to inform clinical decision-making. OpenEvidence (OE) (OpenEvidence, Miami, USA) holds great promise by providing the latest evidence to inform patient care management globally.  Objective To explore the performance of OE in a global context.  Methods Eleven clinicians across six countries, including the United States, Canada, Uruguay, Kenya, Taiwan, and Oman, performed standardized searches for 10 common clinical conditions, with each query identifying the clinician's institution and location. OE search outputs (80 evaluations) were evaluated using the Rubric Assessment Scale (RAS). Additional questions compared US-based results versus other countries. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Differences between US based results and the global group were assessed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test to compare median values as part of an exploratory proof of concept study.  Results OE performed well on core quality metrics. About 88% of the searches were rated as "completely" or "almost entirely" accurate, and 89% were "efficient and succinct" or "mostly efficient," as rated by the authors, with lower scores of 73% for comprehensiveness, 75% for argument and evidence, and 65% for creativity and originality.  US-based searches demonstrated alignment with management guidelines (p=0.02), with higher perceived overall value (p=0.02) and more frequent inclusion of locally authored references by experts (p<0.0001). Greater variability in differential diagnosis was observed in the global group [interquartile ranges (IQR) 1-5 vs 1-2: p=0.03], reflecting wider rater disagreement rather than less relevant differentials, alongside a notable lack of region-specific management recommendations. Of the search results, most references originated in the US, with no Global South references, lacking contextualized management based on regional society guidelines. OE results lacked epidemiologically relevant differentials such as malaria for a febrile child in Kenya. Accessibility to OE was variable, with India lacking access and several Global South countries experiencing variable access.  Conclusion In this exploratory study, OE returned an evidence base that was overwhelmingly US-derived, lacking Global South references, and did not vary with geographic origin of query even when the location was explicitly requested. There was output variability in management suggestions, with US-based searches showing greater alignment with clinical guidelines and locally authored references compared to global searches. These findings are hypothesis-generating and cannot establish causal mechanisms; given the exploratory design and small sample size with convenience sampling, the results should be interpreted cautiously. Clinicians need to critically analyze and evaluate artificial intelligence (AI) outputs and be aware of inherent biases before applying them to clinical practice, especially when caring for patients in global contexts.

title: AI optimized fertilization and irrigation improve wheat yield and quality in semi-arid calcareous soils.
abstract: Traditional wheat farming in calcareous, low-organic-carbon, semi-arid environments relies on blanket fertilization and calendar-based irrigation, causing low nitrogen use efficiency and poor grain quality. We compared traditional practice with an AI-optimized system using soil test-based fertilization and tensiometer-guided irrigation for winter wheat in Khuzestan, Iran. The AI system reduced water use by 12.5% and nitrogen fertilizer by 28% while increasing grain yield by 8.5%. Water productivity improved by 24%, nitrogen use efficiency rose from 43% to 72%, grain protein increased by 13%, zinc by 43%, and iron by 33%. Soil organic carbon increased from 0.42% to 0.48%, microbial biomass carbon increased by 68%, and net greenhouse gas emissions fell by 43%. These findings show that simple, affordable AI tools can support sustainable intensification in semi-arid wheat systems.

title: Bundled AI supported automated breast ultrasound versus handheld ultrasound in organized screening in China.
abstract: Evidence for AI-supported ultrasound screening programs remains limited. We compared a bundled AI-supported automated breast ultrasound (ABUS) workflow with handheld ultrasound (HHUS) in a government-organized screening program. Adjusted risk ratios accounted for baseline imbalance, and standardized cancer detection rate (CDR) accounted for differential biopsy completion. ABUS reduced recall (12.1% vs. 29.9%; adjusted RR 0.45 [95% CI 0.42-0.48]) and biopsy recall (0.99% vs. 2.19%; adjusted RR 0.50 [0.39-0.64]), while increasing biopsy positive predictive value (PPV; 62.1% vs. 20.0%; adjusted RR 2.46 [1.34-4.52]). Observed CDR was higher but not statistically significant (3.08 vs. 1.22 per 1000; adjusted rate ratios 1.90 [0.94-3.86]). Early-stage proportion was higher with ABUS but not statistically significant (84.8% vs. 50.0%; adjusted RR 1.64 [0.71-3.80]). The bundled ABUS pathway was associated with substantially lower recall and higher biopsy PPV. Findings for cancer detection and stage distribution were exploratory because of differential biopsy completion and the small number of cancers.

title: Prediction of coronary artery disease from non-invasive test reports and demographic characteristics using calibrated ensemble learning.
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is commonly confirmed using invasive or imaging-based investigations, motivating transparent prediction from routinely collected clinical information. We analysed 920 records from the Cleveland, Hungarian, Switzerland, and VA Long Beach cohorts of the UCI Heart Disease database. The binary endpoint was absence versus presence of angiographic heart disease. Missing continuous and categorical variables were imputed within training folds, together with fold-contained encoding, scaling, and probability calibration. A stratified split produced 644 development and 276 untouched evaluation records. The primary ensemble averaged sigmoid-calibrated probabilities from K-nearest neighbours, logistic regression, and a support-vector classifier. It achieved accuracy 0.8297, sensitivity 0.8824, specificity 0.7642, precision 0.8232, F1-score 0.8517, AUROC 0.8840, average precision 0.8867, and Brier score 0.1325. A focused comparison of Extra Trees, gradient boosting, histogram gradient boosting, weighted blending, and probability stacking showed that the strongest deterministic and probabilistic models differed: SVC achieved accuracy 0.8333, whereas a constrained blend achieved AUROC 0.8883 and Brier score 0.1299. Permutation importance and Monte Carlo SHAP explanations identified chest-pain type, exercise-induced ST depression, exercise-induced angina, and thallium-test results as influential contributors. Leave-one-cohort-out AUROC ranged from 0.7152 to 0.9011. The combined framework integrates calibrated ensembling, uncertainty quantification, patient-level explanation, and cohort-aware validation for non-invasive CAD prediction.

title: Nurses' Experiences With the Use of Artificial Intelligence-Supported Decision-Making Systems and Their Ethical Dimensions: A Qualitative Study.
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence-supported decision support systems in intensive care units not only improves the quality of care but also supports clinical decision-making processes. However, this transformation raises new ethical issues in nurses' professional roles, ethical responsibilities and human-technology interaction. This study examines in depth the experiences of intensive care nurses regarding the use and ethical dimensions of artificial intelligence-supported decision support systems. The study was conducted as descriptive qualitative research. Data were collected online through semi-structured in-depth interviews and analysed using thematic analysis. The study was conducted with nine nurses who use or have previously used artificial intelligence decision-support systems in hospitals in Türkiye and have at least 2 years of experience in intensive care. The participants' experiences served as the primary data source for understanding how AI-based systems are integrated into the care process and the ethical issues that arise. Approval for the research was obtained from the Ethics Committee of Hacettepe University Social and Human Sciences (11.02.2025/3). Verbal and written consent were obtained from the participants. Analysis of the interviews revealed four contexts and 14 themes. The contexts included 'advantages of system use,' 'limitations,' 'effects of the system on clinical decision-making autonomy' and 'ethical dimension of system use'. The integration of artificial intelligence into nursing is not merely a technological innovation but a significant transformation that reshapes the profession's role and responsibilities. When designed in alignment with nursing values, artificial intelligence can support clinical decision-making, reduce workload and enhance patient safety. However, preserving professional autonomy, ethical responsibility and the human dimension of care must be a fundamental priority throughout this process. For artificial intelligence technologies to be used safely and ethically in clinical settings, it is crucial to protect nurses' professional autonomy, uphold their ethical responsibilities and maintain the human dimension of care. In this regard, the findings provide guidance for integrating artificial intelligence technologies into clinical practice in a manner consistent with nurses' professional values.

title: A multi-dimensional analysis of quality changes in Shandong Junan white tea during storage.
abstract: The chemistry of long-term high-latitude white tea storage remains poorly characterised. This study profiled Junan white tea from newly manufactured tea (Y0) through three years of storage (Y3), using sensory evaluation, colourimetry, electronic-tongue and chemical analyses with multivariate statistics; kinetics were modelled and extrapolated with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). During storage, the made tea turned brownish green and the liquor deepened to dark yellow and orange-red; L* decreased while b* and C* increased; bitterness and astringency attenuated and richness increased. Tea polyphenols and gallic acid, the core markers, changed in opposite directions. Non-esterified catechin C degraded fastest (half-life ≈ 0.98 yr); caffeine showed no detectable change. The PINN offered no accuracy advantage over the kinetic model but extrapolated robustly from sparse data; 5-10-year trajectories await external validation. These results provide an objective basis for year identification and storage management of northern white tea.

title: Recent advances on the alpha-amylase immobilization using nanotechnology: Materials, methods, and applications.
abstract: Alpha-amylase is a critical enzyme in biocatalysis, widely used in industries such as food, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and biofuel production. However, the widespread application of free alpha-amylase is hindered by its limited stability under harsh operational conditions, difficulty in recovery, and single-use nature. The immobilization of alpha-amylase onto nanomaterials has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance its stability, activity, reusability, and overall operational efficiency. This comprehensive review provides an in-depth analysis of recent advancements in this field, systematically evaluating the types of nanomaterials employed, including metal oxides, carbon-based materials, polymers, and advanced hybrid nanocomposites. Key immobilization techniques such as physical adsorption, covalent binding, entrapment, encapsulation, and cross-linking are discussed, highlighting their respective mechanisms, advantages, and limitations. A detailed examination of recent literature demonstrates that nanoengineered immobilization significantly improves thermal stability, pH tolerance, storage stability, and reusability, often with enzymes retaining high activity over many cycles. Furthermore, this review explores the diverse applications of immobilized alpha-amylase across various industrial processes, from food processing and biofuel generation to textile desizing and pharmaceutical synthesis. Finally, current challenges including cost-effectiveness, scalability, toxicity concerns, and enzyme leaching are discussed, alongside future research directions involving artificial intelligence, green synthesis, and smart nanocarrier systems.

title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
abstract: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.

title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
abstract: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.

title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.

title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
abstract: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.
